newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-SRI LANKAN SPINNERS TROUBLE NZ BATSMEN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKAN SPINNERS TROUBLE NZ BATSMEN.

text.p: Sri Lanka's spin bowlers loomed as a threat to New Zealand as early as lunch on the opening day of the second cricket test on Friday as the home side advanced cautiously to 67 for one.
New Zealand went to the break with Blair Pocock on 37 and Matt Horne on 16 after captain Stephen Fleming won the toss and elected to bat first.

The tourists' seam bowlers received minimal assistance from the pitch and captain Arjuna Ranatunga began operating his two off-spinners, Kumar Dharmasena and Muttiah Muralitharan, in tandem from the 22nd over.
Muralitharan, in particular, was able to extract noticeable turn and, with the odd delivery bouncing disconcertingly, Pocock and Horne looked circumspect.
The two spinners gave up just 13 runs in 13 overs between them on a pitch which had previously given generous assistance to the faster bowlers this summer.

Horne could well have lost his wicket on 10, when a ball from Muralitharan bounced and jagged back into him. The ball beat both his bat and the gloves of wicketkeeper Romesh Kaluwitharana when there had been a chance of a stumping.
New Zealand's only wicket to fall was that of opening batsman Bryan Young, who was needlessly run out for four after responding slowly to a call for a single from Pocock.
Young scored a magnificent 267 not out in the first test in Dunedin earlier this week.
